timeline.tweet: Spike is always a mood.
Sometimes I wonder what I would be if my little sister hadn't been around, or if we had grown up elsewhere, in a better environment. Mid-night ponderings, always great. Always the insomniac.
A 2.1/1st mark for my presentation, according to my lecturer. I'm still unsure if it's worth the apprehensiveness, shaky limbs, lowered blood sugars and the griping of the stomach though.
It's been a trugging through treacle kind of day. Slept all day and I'm still exhausted.

To be truly authentic would you have to live your life in solitude? Otherwise, you're just a physical body encompassing experiences in; people known, influenced by, or lost right? Loving the insomnia, yet again 😒

Formative years shouldn't be spent in hiding, but in indulging. Taking in adoration and being engulfed by it. Children shouldn't be raised to be adults that need to get over their childhoods. Nothing will ever anger me as much as the abuse of a child.
All night with the clenching of the stomach and nerves on end. We're in our room, a perfectly safe environment. Mind work with Body to stop being a dumb shit.
All night with the clenching of the stomach and nerves on end. We're in our room, a perfectly safe environment. Mind work with Body to stop being a dumb shit.
Flying out tomorrow to France and my stomach is in knots. I'd sleep, if my heart wasn't beating out of my chest.
Nice morning to watch re-runs of parts of my life apparently. My short term memory needs to chill.
When people clarify this for you too. To "cheer up" or stop seeing them. It's not intentional, but being associated to sadness seems worse than being around.
The idea that someone is used to "get ahead" repulses and saddens me. Wondering if it has happened to the people I respect around me past and present makes me feel physically sick.

The “trust your gut” statement is great until you are in that gut anxiety every day. “Something is wrong”, we don’t know what, but it’s something. My adrenaline and cortisol be flaming like a wild fire. Hyper-vigilance is the only exercise I need to wear me down.
Anxiety so strong my fingers be vibrating.

All day it's like I've been coiled, with my stomach in knots, and a mess in my mind. I'm in a safe space, yet jump whenever a door is closed a little louder than usual. This sense of foreboding is so illogical, yet my body seems on fire. Like electricity in the fingertips.
The point between where my sleeping medication starts to kick in, and falling sleep is what I hope the afterlife Is like (if there is one).
Containing so much anxiety energy is so tiring, there should be a national event post-Brexit where everyone goes to go scream in a wide, open field. I think it’s needed.
I think the majority of my energy is invested in attempting to look "normal" at uni. Inside might be a tempest, but outside I can look like I'm made of stone. Exhausting though.

A night of the worst childhood flashbacks I have ever had. *Calls helpline like I should* “Have a hot drink”. Well shit son, a hot chocolate will solve all the PTSD shit I have had left hanging for 15+ years. Uni was supposed to be better. ‘Foot-Loose-Fancy-Free,I was better’.

I can do the whole “We like to drink with Rhaptitties, ‘cause Rhaptitties is our mate” etc? Is it a scream in an open field kind of night? I’ve got all night- (serial insomniac) and I really love your content, so if I can help in any way...

Lasagne in, floor mopped and sink and hobs sprayed down until they don’t look like last nights dinner was left in them. Work done alongside that as well. I don’t think I’ve had this much energy for years.

Living your life on the verge of mental warfare with yourself perpetually is exhausting. Some hours are white flags and there’s tranquility. Some hours are raging on, caked in mud, with the rain beating down like bullets. Either way, the war is relentless.

Energy for basic things today- 0% Energy for drawing- 50%. At least that’s something.

No-one ever asks how much a person thinks about death as much as they think about their life. The former- whoever you are- I’m an insomniac generally- open into the early hours. I don’t mind a hard conversation.

The abuse of a child angers me to the point my whole body boils, but to me there’s always the especial question as to how someone could do that to their own child. Someone that’s supposed to love their children unconditionally, and they put their children in pain.
Positive: Insomnia allowing me to use the last couple of hours to fill in what seems like 1,000 documents for law related work.

You know it’s exam season when: You wake up in the middle of the night because in your dream you forgot the smallest piece of information and sent you into panic mode. And you just HAVE to check. Sleep evades you. You go beyond stress into a zombie-voodoo like state.

Positive: Question facts for Equity mostly known. I kind of wish my exam was this week, just so it’s out of the way. My body reacts really badly to test season every year; stomach griping, acid reflux, no appetite and nausea. If I don’t study I won’t get a decent mark though 🤷‍♀️

Aftermath of 2nd "proper" EMDR session: Lightheadedness, increase in irritability over seemingly smaller, insignificant things, neutrality in regard to thinking about some past events that used to evoke fearfulness, contrition etc. Tiredness.

Consequences from last EMDR session- sporadic irritability/other spells over insignificant/minor things. Uni is not helping. Work to do seems endless, I can’t talk to my mum about anything that’s going on and I’m getting more and more in a "bubble" with no one else in it.

Over the past 5 or so years I have had meditation recommended to me by multiple services lots of times. Guided meditation with a physical person is fine, but when I try and get into it myself I’m either given my worst thoughts, or it’s like bugs are crawling all over my skin.

Even given 2015 and 2016, I think this is the worst mental health spiral I’ve ever been in. The movies I watch are bland, the food, even my favourites. I’ve filled my head with notes to the brim, but I don’t have the energy for any more of this.
Stomach in knots, vomiting, my sugars all over the place, and dreams about particular cases I’ve been trying to remember? Yup. It’s the last week of exams.
Exhausted. It’s running on 15-20% constantly, regardless of how much rest I get.
Exam season makes me unwell on all accounts; stomach griping and being unable to keep food down and nightmares alongside. I don’t think it’s normal, but it’s been going on for years now.

I keep thinking of late that there’s something off with me socially. As in sometimes (the hospital this week) eye contact is painful and I can’t hold it. My legs shake-like a calming technique. I prefer my own company over obligatory talk and it’s exhausting if I do "small talk".
All the time- Sometimes I get a little rise in my chest, or a thump a little too fast, but a general “I can't wait for this” unadulterated excitement doesn't happen to me. You're not alone.
Isolation, Desperation, Unrequited Love
Such an insult to injury- rage all you like, with full entitlement to it.

I don’t quite know how to articulate it to friends, family, acquaintances etc without coming across as really aloof, but I have a limit on social interaction and when I exceed that limit I need to isolate before I burst. It gets so exhausting being with people for me.

Results are out this time tomorrow and throughout the night my heart has been beating out of my chest. Sleep disturbance, reflux, stomach ache- the physical and the mental always come side by side when I’m an anxious mess.

Positive: I’ve been having a lot of nightmares recently, for no particular reason. My cat can seemingly “sense” them as he always sits with me after I wake up, and nuzzles me to make it a little better 🐱💕
Working on a how anxiety feels for me mental health piece. Really hyper-vigilant, all eyes on you, inundated by overthinking every thought, knots in the stomach etc.
Thank you 😊 It’s a mental health piece based on anxiety; knots in the stomach, apprehensive thoughts, clouded judgements etc.
Lawful irritable 🤘

Until I went through PTSD analysis, I was so unaware as to how much energy I have invested in flight or fight from a young age. It explains my general avoidance of people, given the perpetual surveying of threat- it’s exhausting to just be around others.

My cat and crosswords. When my brain is going a mile a minute and I can’t focus on reading, having the tranquil environment of my pet and a grounding for my brain and rampant flashbacks/triggers is really useful.

Sounds utterly exhausting. It might not help you, but when I know that when I’m out I’ll be hit by every anxious thought, I take someone with me. Even if we’re just out a few minutes, it’s getting out.

I was doing some research because the mood is low and the insomnia is on fire, and I came across the uni that some places still have suicide criminalised. The authorities then put the individuals up for the death penalty. Wellll you’ve given people what they wanted 🙄👏👏
Yup, but ignoring it just makes it more potent. I try to place that energy into something else; video games, art, walking etc. The insidious effect is really irritating though.
Insomnia got the better of me tonight, but I have finished 2 Vac applications and 3 for Chambers...
I know there’s still the argument present that Anxiety is just “a mental thing.” The stomach cramping/griping, acid reflux, and shakiness are just coincidences then right?!
I know there’s still the argument present that Anxiety is just “a mental thing.” The stomach cramping/griping, acid reflux, and shakiness are just coincidences then right?!
There are so many beverages that pair well with Anxiety. Are you going sophisticated (Wine, Gin etc), or going for a good time (Rum, Vodka etc)?

Shakiness with atrocious motor control (spilling things, knocking things over, looking somewhat intoxicated sometimes🙃), big fluctuations in hot/cold feelings within the space of half an hour, and general fatigue.

I’m aware of so many Law students that push themselves to the edge (myself included) in the idea of getting an extra bit done. I’ve been prescribed Zopiclone (short term) due to pushing myself into an insomniac pattern again. The culture of Law and Legal studies isn’t healthy.

I understand why the courts deal with Domestic Violence in the Civil and Criminal courts, but it makes me angry that more Domestic Abusers are given orders, than prison time. I’d argue it has similarities to ABH, GBH? Maybe I’m too biased in how things (didn’t) happen for me.
Same. There’s always more to do, and so, the crying is scheduled now.

Some nights I go over the fact that £1.5 million is the loss incurred for your reputation (Yorkshire Ripper case) and £3,500 is the loss of a mother, sister, friend etc due to Medical Negligence. It was the first time studying I was so angry I threw the book down.

“Have you tried a hot drink”, “Maybe it’s lack of sleep”. When you pluck up the courage to phone a stranger and then get shut down is debilitating. Sometimes it’s this and the sad seeming to pollute everyone else in your real life and they don’t want to be around you either.
What is the most terrifying is the idea of the NHS crumbling and the insulin-dependant being forced to keep themselves alive through their own pockets.

The energy is taken out of you in the perpetual explaining of your current position, or attempting to "legitimise" your feelings, in the gamble that your points won’t be misconstrued and just accepted as they are. Which is bizarre that you almost have to apologise for feeling.

If it’s a stuffed nose or flu type symptoms, hot showers to clear the nasal passage, with some lavender dropped on the pillow before sleep. Hot soups as well; chunky vegetable is my favourite when I don’t have the energy to make anything. Meds too like general paracetamol.

No-one ever seems to talk about menstrual flooding: The soaked sheets, inability to move/work on account of cramping and constantly analysing yourself for clots where ever you go. It feels so shameful to have something my body is supposed to go through, but in overdrive.
Over here as well. I just can’t calm my mind down at all lately. Very clip show currently. Meditation makes my skin seem like it has bugs crawling over me, so that’s a dud for sleep mode too🙃😬

Mood swings in relation to triggers. I’m having a fairly OK day and then an auditory flashback occurs, which leaves me sensitised to sound for the rest of the day. It’s like being an open sore after that🙃
Reading, but when concentration has failed me on that, cooking and going on my Switch. Cooking especially as I can do it for other people as well.

My concentration has diminished considerably post-exams. I’m used to finishing books within the same day and now I can barely go 100 pages without needing to walk around. The wait between sitting exams and getting the results has led to a nervous energy I can’t quell.

Whilst dealing with c-PTSD, I have found that some chunks of my childhood are missing from my memory. My sister and mum can remember events, whilst I have no recollection, but was apparently there. From my research, the hippocampus is affected by trauma; It’s disconcerting.
15. Over the course of my GCSEs, my mental health went down its first downward spiral. I was told by my parents that it was "all in your head". 2 years later, I was diagnosed with Depression.

I realise this might be a long shot, but does anyone have any advice on how to handle fluctuating emotions in suspected BPD (Borderline Personality Disorder)? The uncontrollable anger over anything. I don’t want to make things worse by tackling it wrong.

Positive: I’m starting therapy again on Friday, following a relapse in mental health related to nightmares and flashbacks. Now that I’m not going back to uni until October, I have time to work on myself over the summer.

Sad is fleeting (a moment, or just a bad day for me) depressed is an every day melancholy/numbness/apathy for weeks on end. Everything is flat when depression sets in, I could receive the best news whilst depressed and it wouldn’t change anything. My sadness is adjustable.

I’m proud to say that even with low energy, I have still been able to work on these: One sketch a day seems to be working for me.

Sometimes it’s as though suicide is only legitimate around the time the particular awareness month comes around too. It isn’t just September-October that can be "kind months". Suicidal people don’t have a clock in which to say, well that period is up now, back to being alright.

-Losing the thread of conversations- not out of boredom, just the inability to concentrate. -Crying without a cause. -Depression naps to do something other than focus on what is going on throughout the day. -Regardless of the amount of sleep, everything is exhausting.
